answer.rationale: The scenario describes a multi-employer worksite under HazCom where one employer's chemicals may expose another employer's workers. §1910.1200(e)(2) directly requires the hazard communication program to address methods for informing other employers on-site of SDS access and precautionary/labeling information. This builds on the baseline requirement to develop and maintain a written hazard communication program (e)(1), and the program must be made available upon request (e)(4). No PSM-specific facts (e.g., covered chemical process, NAICS industry) are given, so PSM contractor-related requirements are not applicable here.
